label: TP-Link Omada SG2008P
description: Fanless 8-port Gigabit smart switch: 8x 1G RJ45, 802.3at/af PoE+ on ports 1-4 against a 62 W budget.

poe.note: Vendor table, row "PoE Ports (RJ45)": "Standard: 802.3af/at compliant / PoE Ports: 4 Ports / Power Supply: 62 W*" (https://www.omadanetworks.com/us/business-networking/omada-switch-access/sg2008p/, HTTP 200, 187,036 B, read 2026-11-21); the same page's summary line calls it "62 W Power Budget" and the interface row says "8x 10/100/1000 Mbps RJ45 Ports (Ports 1-4 Support 802.3at/af PoE+)". The 62 W is the PD-side allowance, not the adapter's rating: the adapter row is "AC/DC Adapter (Input: 100-240V AC; Output: 53.5V DC/1.31A)" = 70.1 W, and "Max. Power Consumption: 73.4 W (220 V/50 Hz @ 25 C) (with 62 W PD connected)" - 62 W of PD load plus about 11 W of chassis. Four 802.3af loads (4 x 15.4 W = 61.6 W) fit; four class-4 25.5 W loads (102 W) do not, and the allocator refuses the third.

notes: PoE is the whole point of this SKU and the spec had none of it: the description promised "4 PoE+ ports and 62 W power budget" while every port carried no poeOut and the capabilities list omitted poe-pse, so `show power inline` answered "% No PoE on ...: no port on this device can supply power" for a switch sold as a PoE switch. Fixed against the vendor table quoted in poe.note: ports 1-4 source 802.3at/af (PoE+), against a 62 W budget. Ports 5-8 are declared poeOut:false rather than left silent, because engine/media.js fills a silent poeOut on every RJ45 port of a switch that claims poe-pse - a silence here would have invented four more PSE ports and let a lab cable a powered device into a port that has no power supply behind it. The vendor's own max-consumption row (73.4 W with 62 W of PD attached) is what makes 62 W the PoE budget rather than a PSU rating. research/tp-link-sg2008p-poe-budget.md carries the quotes.
